brief.recommendation: Checkout success collapsed to 0% (BIZ-4) with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The blocker (batch_replayable_coupon_expiry_sweep) is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt policy, 8-min replay cost, 950s typical runtime (BIZ-2). No protected settlements (DB-2) and no change-calendar restriction (BIZ-3). Trade-off analysis shows waiting 946s remaining costs ~$290,045 and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-5). Memory shows 4/4 prior terminations of similar batch_replayable jobs restored checkout to 100% (MEM-1). Terminating is the only action that fits within business tolerance.

audit.report: The coupon_expiry_sweep batch job (pid 1309276) went idle in transaction for 4.2s holding locks that blocked 12 checkout sessions, collapsing checkout success to 0% with $18,400/min revenue at risk. Both guardians agreed to terminate the blocker: it is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt policy, 8-minute replay cost, no protected settlements, and no change-calendar restrictions. The trade-off favored termination (waiting 946s more would cost ~$290K vs 8-min replay). The executor terminated the process, but verification failed because a new instance (pid 1309887) of the same job immediately restarted and again went idle in transaction for 7.5s, blocking checkout at 25% success. The incident is escalated.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_coupon_expiry_sweep job runs for ~950s, goes idle in transaction holding locks, and automatically restarts after termination, immediately re-blocking checkout.
lessons: For coupon_expiry_sweep: add a scheduler pause/disable mechanism so termination during incidents prevents immediate restart and re-blocking.
For coupon_expiry_sweep: investigate why the job goes idle in transaction (last statement SELECT 1) for seconds — this idle hold is the direct cause of checkout lock contention.
For coupon_expiry_sweep: consider reducing lock scope or adding a statement_timeout to prevent long idle-in-transaction periods.
audit.negotiation_critique: The guardians negotiated correctly in one round (161.8s): Database Guardian gathered all required evidence (workload registry, protected settlements, change calendar, business impact, memory of prior successes) and Continuity Guardian accepted without objection. No rounds were wasted and no evidence was missed. The negotiation was sound but the action was insufficient because the job scheduler restarted the blocker.
follow_ups: Engineering to investigate why coupon_expiry_sweep executes SELECT 1 and idles in transaction for seconds — fix the application logic or add statement_timeout.
Platform to implement a 'pause scheduler' control for batch_replayable_coupon_expiry_sweep so incident termination sticks.
Review whether coupon_expiry_sweep should remain BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt given its 950s runtime and tendency to idle-hold locks.
